question: to the Commission Tilly Metz (Verts/ALE) Subject:

Media reports1 allege that almost 1 000 poultry farms in Poland are operating without the permits required under Directive 2010/75/EU on industrial emissions (IED). It is further reported that some of these farms have caused environmental damage and water pollution, allegedly in breach of Articles 4, 5 and 14 IED, with negative impacts on the health and wellbeing of local communities. According to reports, Poland’s Chief Inspectorate for Environmental Protection asked all regional inspectorates to review their records and determine how many industrial poultry farms require permits under the IED. It is understood that this exercise found that around 80 % of the farms operating without permits were in fact large enough to require one. In the light of the above, can the Commission answer the following: 1.
Is it aware of the scale of non-compliance with the IED by industrial poultry farms in Poland, and can it confirm the findings reported by the Polish authorities?
What assessment has the Commission made of the environmental and public health impact of these alleged breaches?
What action does it intend to take to ensure compliance with EU environmental law and effective enforcement by the Polish authorities?
https://www.thebureauinvestigates.com/stories/2026-03-31/polands-packed-ghost-farms-present-thedanger-of-undetected-disease 1
answer: EN on behalf of the European Commission (16.7.2026) The Commission is aware of the allegations1 about non-compliance of poultry farms in Poland with the Industrial Emissions Directive2 (IED) as in March 2026, a complaint on that issue was submitted to the Commission and is currently under analysis. The Commission notes that it is primarily for the Member States to ensure the correct application of and full compliance with EU environmental legislation, including the IED and its provisions on inspections and compliance assurance. The Commission services have reached out to the Polish authorities and asked for further information. Any decisions on the potential follow up and action to be taken will be made once the analysis is finalised. The Commission also notes that, in February 2024, an infringement case for non-conform transposition of some of the IED provisions was opened against Poland3. The case covers ninety grievances and the analysis of the Polish reply to the letter of formal notice is underway. Further steps will be decided after the assessment of the reply is finalised.
